about: The MCP clients whose client ID metadata documents (CIMD, the MCP spec's Client ID Metadata Documents; 6E3c, AG5) the API fetches, in one place: the foundation opens the apps subnet's way out to each one's addresses on 443 (network.bicep) and lets the network look up its host (dns-policy.bicep), and the apps deployment puts its origin on the API's outbound allowlist and its entry on AGENTX_OAUTH_CLIENT_METADATA_ORIGINS wherever Agent X's OAuth server is on (apps.bicep). Adding a client is one entry here: `metadata` is what the API trusts, written as the setting takes it (an origin, a path prefix ending in `/`, or one document's exact address; https, lowercase, as the URL parser prints it); `prefixes` are the IPv4 ranges its host answers from, as its owner publishes them, with `source` saying where; the host's name is read from `metadata`. Any client not listed registers itself (RFC 7591, DCR), as every client could before. The API's own guards stay as they are (oauth-client-metadata.ts): only listed addresses fetched, only origins on its allowlist, no redirect followed, 3 seconds and 16 KB at most. A range shared by many sites (Cloudflare's) lets the subnet reach those sites by address, as Front Door's tag does for email: the API's exact origins and the DNS policy's names are the real limit. Checked by mcp-clients.test.ts and the policy's apps-egress and dns-allow rules.

clients.source: Anthropic's published inbound addresses, which claude.ai answers from: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/ip-addresses (checked 19 Nov 2026)
